title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 173 (Pawnee’s right of retainer)

content.overview: Section 173 provides that the pawnee may retain the goods pledged, not only for payment of the debt or the performance of the promise, but for the interest of the debt, and all necessary expenses incurred by him in respect of the possession or for the preservation of the goods pledged.
content.glance: Pawnee may retain the goods for the debt or promise, interest on the debt, and necessary expenses for possession or preservation.
content.study: The pawnee may retain the goods pledged, not only for payment of the debt or the performance of the promise, but for the interest of the debt, and all necessary expenses incurred by him in respect of the possession or for the preservation of the goods pledged. Current-law framing: retainer covers principal, interest and necessary preservation/possession expenses.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The pawnee may retain the goods pledged, not only for payment of the debt or the performance of the promise, but for the interest of the debt, and all necessary expenses incurred by him in respect of the possession or for the preservation of the goods pledged.

examples.title: Retainer for interest and expenses
examples.body: Pawnee retains pledged goods not only for the principal debt but also for interest and necessary preservation expenses under Section 173.

hypotheticals.question: May the pawnee retain the goods for interest and necessary expenses in addition to the debt?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 173 expressly permits retainer for the debt or promise, the interest of the debt, and necessary expenses for possession or preservation.
